mainEntity.name: How long do veneers on incisal edges last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Porcelain veneers are generally considered durable and, with good oral hygiene and regular dental care, may last many years. The longevity of veneers on incisal edges can be affected by factors such as dietary habits, whether a patient grinds their teeth, and how well the veneers are maintained. Patients who grind their teeth may be advised to wear a protective night guard. Your dental professional can give you a more realistic indication of expected durability based on your individual circumstances during a clinical consultation.

mainEntity.name: Will veneers damage my natural teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Traditional porcelain veneers typically require a small amount of enamel to be removed from the tooth surface to ensure the veneer sits flush and does not look bulky. This preparation is permanent, which is why it is important to make an informed decision before proceeding. Composite veneers and bonding techniques may require little or no tooth preparation in some cases. Your dentist will discuss the preparation process clearly with you before any treatment is undertaken, so you can make a fully informed decision.

mainEntity.name: Can uneven incisal edges be fixed without veneers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in many cases. Depending on the extent and cause of the unevenness, options such as composite bonding, dental recontouring, or orthodontic treatment may be considered. Composite bonding is a minimally invasive approach that may help reshape chipped or worn incisal edges and, in many cases, requires little or no tooth preparation compared with traditional veneer techniques. The most suitable approach will be determined during a clinical examination once the underlying cause of the irregularity has been assessed properly.

mainEntity.name: Is it painful to have veneers placed?

acceptedAnswer.text: The placement of dental veneers is not generally a painful procedure. Local anaesthetic is typically used during any preparation of the tooth surface, and the bonding process itself is not associated with discomfort. Some patients experience mild sensitivity in the days following veneer placement, particularly at the incisal edge, but this usually settles. If you have concerns about the procedure, discussing them openly with your dental professional beforehand will allow them to explain each step and address any anxieties.

mainEntity.name: Can veneers fix incisal edges that have been worn down by teeth grinding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Veneers may be considered as part of a treatment plan for wear caused by bruxism, but it is generally important to address the grinding itself first. If veneers are placed without managing the underlying bruxism, there is a risk of the restorations themselves becoming damaged over time. A bite guard (occlusal splint) is often recommended to protect both natural teeth and any restorations. Your dental professional will assess your bite and discuss a comprehensive treatment plan tailored to your situation.

mainEntity.name: How much do veneers cost for uneven incisal edges?

acceptedAnswer.text: Veneer costs vary depending on the material used (porcelain or composite), the number of teeth being treated, and the complexity of the case. As a private dental treatment in London, costs should always be discussed transparently during a consultation, and a written treatment plan with fees should be provided before any work is agreed upon. It is worth asking about all available options at different price points so you can make an informed decision that aligns with both your dental needs and your budget.
